text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.3% today to $144.96, giving back gains from the past week as oil prices dropped on hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict. Crude has fallen for a second consecutive day after U.S. and Iranian leadership signaled openness to negotiations, easing concerns about supply disruptions that had pushed prices higher earlier in the week. The stock hit $154 just three trading days ago when geopolitical tensions were running hotter.

The broader refining picture is more mixed. Competitors like Saudi Aramco and BP are posting record profits as refining margins have widened during the conflict — the spread between crude costs and refined product prices has expanded enough to boost their bottom lines significantly. For an integrated producer like ConocoPhillips, lower crude prices can offset some benefit from strong refining economics, which may explain why the stock is retreating even while refiners are celebrating their results.
